hypotheses: Connected simple triangle-free 5-regular graph on 32 vertices, diameter exactly eight, with a fixed diametral eight-geodesic. The complete graph has exactly q middle vertices, all isolated in F. The general correspondence treats q=1,2,3; the principal template theorem treats q=2.
mathematical_checks: The independent 15-set and five-edge defect follow from center distances and degree sums. An L-R edge shortens the diametral path to five; a B vertex meeting both sides shortens it to six. Thus every port has all r=4-q side neighbors on one side. Isolated middle vertices have exactly B as neighborhood. Four such vertices close a forbidden K5,5 component.

For a side, five omitted (n-4)-sets are precisely the complements of the four independent endpoint-row neighborhoods; each omitted set covers every internal edge. Independent port r-sets and the equation o(x)-k(x)=d_D(x) express exact degree five. The bound o(x)<=4 expresses genuine side membership. With the now explicit basic bounds and nonempty port parts, the converse is connected through the common endpoint center and H, and introduces no triangle or parallel graph edge.

For q=2, side sizes sum to twelve and each is at least five. A five-side would have 25=20+2b+2e, an odd-even contradiction. Therefore both sides have six vertices, e(D)+b=5 and maximum internal degree two. The path/cycle exhaustion is complete. The excluded path forests either have independence number three or force a positive-degree vertex into all five endpoint rows, exceeding degree five. Exactly the five printed shapes survive.

The automatic diameter proof is valid for every admissible table. Let S be the union of port-pair supports. A row disjoint from S forces S to be its omitted two-cover; since D has an edge and S is independent, a crossing edge gives distance four to any H vertex. A side vertex outside S either shares a row with S, has an internal edge to S, or would force every row to omit S, contradicting side membership. All vertices are within four of every H twin; the two endpoint centers have minimum distance four. Removing H separates the sides, giving distance exactly eight and a universal upper bound eight.

The construction has a four-cycle from two H vertices and two ports. Every internal edge has endpoints with nonempty disjoint endpoint-row neighborhoods, giving a five-cycle through the endpoint center. Hence girth is exactly four and every q=2 template is nonbipartite. The designated centers realize the exact two-isolated-middle profile.

The one-port C4 side has only opposite-pair covers, with U multiplicities two and three and V equal to the triple-cover pair. For a two-port P4 side, the cover pairs are 13,23,24. Solving the degree equations gives V multiplicities 3-c,a+c-4,3-a and the stated constraints; reflection leaves precisely the three printed rooted side types.

For the matching three-port side, both U and V use cross-pairs between the two internal edges. The four margin differences equal one, and U degrees are automatically at most four. For the path three-port side, all two-covers are uw or v paired with one other vertex. The conditions 1<=t<=3 and equations (8)-(9) give exactly all permitted independent V pairs and their degrees. No attachment is omitted.

For the four-port side, every U pair meets u or v. If its internal-edge multiplicity is x and V has z isolate-isolate edges, degree totals give z=1-x. Thus x is zero or one. Equations (11) and (12), including the isolated omission-degree upper bound, are necessary and sufficient; the x=0 form has exactly one isolate-isolate edge. Loops and the forbidden uv port pair remain excluded.

The full weighted quotient by equality of open neighborhoods is intrinsic and exactly reconstructs the graph by independent blow-up. Ordinary isomorphism is equivalent to weighted quotient isomorphism, without root or side colors. The size bounds 1+6+16=23 and 1+10+15=26 count guaranteed twin collapses; additional twins only lower these bounds. The number 26 is not an ordinary class count.

In the explicit example, the two-port side has ten full neighborhood classes. The three-port path side satisfies t=1,a=1,c=0,z_i=z_j=z_k=1 and V=[uk]+[vi]+[vj]. Its five row supports and three port supports are distinct; the internal path degrees, different row degrees and distinct isolate row/port supports distinguish all fifteen side vertices. Opposite-side J classes cannot coincide because each meets its own endpoint neighborhood; I and J classes cannot coincide because every J vertex has an I neighbor while N(I) lies in J. Thus the example has exactly 10+15+1=26 full classes, ordinarily different from the M=3 examples with 15 and 16.
